Results.ReviewText:
This is actually our first gas grill and we're very happy with it. It is solidly built and we expect it to last for years. We've only had it for a little over a month, but have used it several times and it has worked well each time. 
I could have bought one pre-assembled, but I wanted to put it together myself not only to know how it was put together but also to know it was done right. I used a combination of the written instructions and the "Bilt" video and had not problems. I like the new "Bilt" videos as you can rotate the images in any direction to see what it should look like when done.
I also bought some accessories to go with it, including Weber's cover, rotisserie and light. The cover fits well with Velcro in several places to help keep it from blowing away when it is windy and the light is pretty cool in that it comes on when you lift the cover but can also be removed to use independently. I do have to say it is certainly on the pricey side. Haven't tried the rotisserie yet but plan to soon.
Back to the grill....
The wing tables are nice to have and include three hooks on each side for hanging tools. The stainless steel, however, does scratch easily but it's not really a problem.
I like the hanging tank gauge that quickly shows the amount of propane that is left. It's easy to see what the level is and easy to attach the tank.
The starter works quickly too. Turn on the gas, and as soon as the start button is pushed the fire is lit. Don't know how long the battery will last yet.
We've had Weber grills (charcoal) for several years now and they still work fine. I've used a Smokey Joe for camping and we still have our full sized kettle grill that has plenty of miles on it. This is partly why we chose another Weber.
While I can't testify to the longevity of this grill, I can say that we're happy with it so far.
Results.Title: Good looking and good working grill!
